patient.chief_complaint: New seizure-like episodes over the past 2 months — different from prior epileptic seizures
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. F is a 42-year-old truck driver with established right temporal lobe epilepsy, seizure-free on levetiracetam for 4 years, who presents with 2-month history of new episodes that he and his wife describe as different from his prior seizures. His prior epileptic seizures consisted of right temporal aura (déjà vu, rising epigastric sensation), followed by unresponsiveness with oral automatisms (lip smacking, swallowing) lasting 60-90 seconds, and post-ictal confusion for 5-10 minutes. The new episodes are distinctly different: they consist of bilateral whole-body shaking with arched back (opisthotonus-like posturing), closed eyes, 2-5 minute duration, no post-ictal confusion, and immediate full recovery. His wife is convinced these are different from his prior seizures. His driving license was suspended when he reported new episodes, creating significant financial and psychological stress as trucking is his sole income source. He is desperate to have the episodes attributed to epilepsy (which is treatable and would support his disability claim) rather than to a functional cause. Levetiracetam level was checked by his PCP and was therapeutic. He has been compliant with medications. Prior MRI from 3 years ago showed right mesial temporal sclerosis (MTS). His diabetes is well-controlled. He has not had any prior PNES episodes.

background.description: Slightly increased theta activity over right temporal region (F8, T4, T8) — consistent with right MTS substrate. Otherwise normal background.

findings.type: Whole-body shaking episode — 3 min 12 sec (the new episode type)
findings.morphology: No ictal pattern during the entire clinical episode. Right temporal interictal sharp-and-slow-wave activity continues unchanged. No ictal evolution, no spread, and no post-ictal electrodecrement. The captured event had no ictal EEG correlate.

eeg.impression: This is an ABNORMAL EEG. Right temporal interictal sharp-and-slow-wave discharges, unchanged in character from prior study. One clinical event captured during the recording showed no ictal EEG correlate; normal background maintained throughout the event and post-event period. No post-event slowing recorded

clinical_assessment.impression: The phenotype is paroxysmal rather than motor, so limb rule-in signs do not apply. The semiological features documented are: Arched-back (opisthotonus-like) posturing during events. Semiology is suggestive but not sufficient: for this phenotype the positive diagnostic act is a recorded habitual event without EEG correlate, which is why video-EEG is required in this case rather than optional.

interactions: Levetiracetam is known to cause irritability, depression, and behavioral changes in 5-15% of patients. This may be contributing to mood symptoms.
Sertraline + levetiracetam: no pharmacokinetic interaction. Safe combination.
warnings: If mood side effects from levetiracetam are prominent, consider switching to alternative AED (lamotrigine has mood-stabilizing properties and is a good alternative for temporal lobe epilepsy)
Do not discontinue levetiracetam abruptly — seizure risk
alternatives: Lamotrigine as alternative AED with mood-stabilizing benefit

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Functional neurological disorder — PNES superimposed on established right temporal lobe epilepsy (mixed epilepsy + PNES)

differential.key_features: Witnessed convulsive-appearing events; ictal video-EEG showing absence of electrographic correlate during a captured habitual event is the key differentiator.
Focal complaints warrant imaging; normal brain MRI without lesion, mass, or enhancement effectively excludes a structural cause for the presenting deficit.
Episodic neurological symptoms can occur in autoimmune encephalitis; normal MRI, normal EEG background, and (when obtained) negative antibody panel render this very unlikely.

FND is involuntary; preserved effort on symptom-validity testing and absence of clear secondary gain argue against feigning. The rule-in signs do not distinguish FND from malingering by themselves, but the clinical context does not support a feigning explanation.

useless_tools.rationale: ECG has no diagnostic role in FND; cardiac etiology is not on the differential for the presenting neurological deficit.
Echocardiography has no role in FND; no structural cardiac question is raised by the presentation.
Cardiac rhythm monitoring is not indicated; the events are non-syncopal and the rule-in signs point to FND.
Non-contrast head CT adds no information beyond MRI for an FND workup and contributes diagnostic noise plus radiation exposure.
Lumbar puncture is not indicated in typical FND; invasive testing reinforces somatic illness model and adds iatrogenic risk without changing management.
Advanced PET imaging has no indication in FND; standard MRI is the appropriate structural workup.

Nerve conduction studies and EMG have no role once positive functional signs are documented: the deficit is not neuromuscular, the study is uncomfortable, and a normal result reinforces the patient's search for an organic cause — the principal iatrogenic harm in this condition
Somatosensory evoked potentials answer a question about a lesion in the somatosensory pathway; a midline-splitting, non-anatomical sensory deficit is not that question

critical_actions: Document the event semiology and the features atypical for an epileptic seizure; the diagnosis is established by capturing a habitual event on video-EEG, not by a limb sign
Obtain video-EEG capturing a habitual event with normal interictal EEG to confirm PNES
Communicate the diagnosis transparently using positive language and the rule-in signs as the basis
Refer for FND-informed physiotherapy and CBT / psychological therapy
Order a comprehensive neuropsychological battery to characterize comorbid depression, anxiety, somatization, and trauma exposure — informs treatment planning (criteria-pack 'recommended' tier)

Communicate the diagnosis transparently using positive language anchored on the rule-in signs; explicitly state the diagnosis is FND, the symptoms are real and involuntary, and there is an evidence-based treatment plan
Refer to specialized FND-informed physiotherapy (for functional motor symptoms) and to CBT / psychological therapy (for PNES and comorbid mood / anxiety)
contraindicated_actions: Do not pursue ever-expanding negative investigations — per Stone 2018, repeated negative workups reinforce illness conviction and worsen prognosis
Do not frame the diagnosis as 'all in your head', 'nothing wrong', or 'we couldn't find anything' — this damages the therapeutic alliance and is the most common avoidable harm in FND
Do not perform invasive testing (lumbar puncture, nerve biopsy, muscle biopsy, cerebral angiography) when positive rule-in signs are present and there is no clinical indication
Do not order EMG/NCS, muscle biopsy, or nerve biopsy as part of an FND workup — these invasive tests reinforce the somatic illness model per Stone 2018
Do not start or continue long-term anti-epileptic drugs for functional (psychogenic non-epileptic) seizures — AEDs are ineffective for PNES and expose the patient to side effects
Do not give benzodiazepines as abortive therapy for witnessed PNES events (no benefit and risk of respiratory depression)
Do not give gadolinium without a specific indication — contrast adds cost and risk and answers no question that positive functional signs have not already answered

Do not repeat the brain MRI, the laboratory panel or the lumbar puncture once a first normal study and positive rule-in signs are documented: each repetition strengthens the patient's belief that something organic has been missed
key_reasoning_points: FND is a positive diagnosis based on rule-in signs (Hoover, tremor entrainment, give-way weakness, non-dermatomal sensory loss with midline split) — not a diagnosis of exclusion (Espay 2018, Stone 2018).

Brain MRI and basic laboratory testing are OPTIONAL here, not due diligence: the diagnosis rests on the positive signs, and each additional negative study is a cost and an iatrogenic harm rather than a confirmation. Where imaging is recommended in this case it is for one specific alternative question, once.
Over-investigation is the principal iatrogenic harm in FND; every additional negative test reinforces the patient's illness conviction and worsens prognosis (Stone 2018).
Psychiatric comorbidity (anxiety, depression, trauma) is common and informs treatment planning but is NOT required for the diagnosis and does not 'explain' the symptoms in a reductive sense.
Diagnostic communication matters: using positive language anchored on the rule-in signs is associated with better engagement and outcomes (Stone 2018).
Evidence-based treatment is multidisciplinary — CBT for PNES and FND-informed physiotherapy for functional motor symptoms (Nielsen 2015).
Video-EEG capturing a habitual event with normal interictal EEG is diagnostic for PNES (ILAE PNES Task Force 2013); routine EEG alone is insufficient.

Interim composition decision, August 2026: FND remains only to keep the frozen dataset at 20 conditions/600 cases. The positive functional-neurological examination is the sole required diagnostic act; every instrumental test is optional and case-targeted. DLB remains the preferred future replacement when composition work resumes.

red_herrings.data_point: Family history of epilepsy in a relative
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on an epileptic etiology and pursue prolonged AED trials before confirming PNES with video-EEG
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Family history of epilepsy does not establish the patient's events as epileptic. Video-EEG capturing the habitual event without ictal correlate is the gold standard.

red_herrings.data_point: Symptom onset coincident with a major psychosocial stressor
red_herrings.intended_effect: Conclude prematurely that stress 'caused' the symptoms and that the workup can be abbreviated
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Many organic conditions (MS, migraine, epilepsy) also flare with stress. Stress at onset is supportive context, not a diagnostic substitute for the positive rule-in signs.
